pr.title: panic when an interpreter error gets unintentionally discarded
pr.description:
One important invariant of Miri is that when an interpreter error is raised (*in particular* a UB error), those must not be discarded: it's not okay to just check `foo().is_err()` and then continue executing.

This seems to catch new contributors by surprise fairly regularly, so this PR tries to make it so that *if* this ever happens, we get a panic rather than a silent missed UB bug. The interpreter error type now contains a "guard" that panics on drop, and that is explicitly passed to `mem::forget` when an error is deliberately discarded.

Fixes https://github.com/rust-lang/miri/issues/3855
pr.author: RalfJung

analysis.summary: Historical compiler PR enforces that interpreter errors raised during speculative const evaluation in DataflowConstProp, GVN, JumpThreading, and KnownPanicsLint must never be silently swallowed. The interpreter result type gains a drop guard that panics unless the error is explicitly discarded, propagated, or reported; pass sites that previously consumed InterpResult via plain `.ok()`/implicit drop now call `.discard_err()`, while combined fallible operations use `and` to make error precedence explicit.
analysis.originalLogic: These MIR passes speculatively invoke InterpCx operations and treat an interpreter error as a conservative fallback: DataflowConstProp maps cast/unary/binary failures to `FlatSet::Top` via `int_to_int_or_float(...).map_or(FlatSet::Top, ...)` and uses `.ok()?` on projections/discriminants/constants; GVN uses `.ok()?` on `eval_mir_constant`, field/variant projections, binary/unary ops, casts, and allocation operations; JumpThreading uses `.ok()`/`.ok()?` on the same projection and constant-eval helpers; KnownPanicsLint's `use_ecx` converts an interpreter error to `None` after tracing and asserting. The old implementation discarded the resulting `InterpErrorInfo` with `.ok()`, `.is_err()`, or an implicit drop and continued with a conservative value.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Consuming an `InterpResult` from an InterpCx operation with a plain `.ok()`/`.is_err()` or by dropping the result without exhausting it, thereby silently discarding the interpreter error (which may be UB or an unsupported operation) instead of explicitly marking the discard with `.discard_err()`, propagating it with `?`, or reporting it with `.report_err()`. In the fixed implementation each intended discard is explicit (`int_to_int_or_float(&op, layout).discard_err()`, `eval_mir_constant(...).discard_err()?`, `project_field(...).discard_err()`), and merely dropping an unconsumed `InterpResult` triggers the new guard panic.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies, constants, and generic instantiations where a speculative InterpCx operation returns `Err`: out-of-bounds or invalid index/field projections, invalid enum discriminants/niches, invalid casts, arithmetic failures, uninitialized reads, unimplemented/failed constant evaluation, and paths where two interpreter errors can co-occur (stack-frame pop plus return-value copy; allocation access plus misalignment check).
analysis.trigger: A pass consumes a failed `InterpResult` without exhausting it, e.g. `expr.ok()`, `expr.is_err()`, or letting the result fall out of scope, rather than calling `discard_err()`, using `?`, or `report_err()`. The new drop guard then panics with "an interpreter error got improperly discarded; use `discard_err()` if this is intentional".
preconditions: The compiler includes the guarded InterpResult type whose Drop panics when an error-containing result is dropped unconsumed.
The optimized program drives a MIR optimization pass (DataflowConstProp, GVN, JumpThreading, or KnownPanicsLint) to evaluate an InterpCx operation that returns Err.
The pass takes the conservative fallback path (Top/None/unknown) rather than propagating the interpreter error as a compile error.
pitfalls: `.discard_err()` intentionally ignores the error and yields `Option<T>`; it is only correct when ignoring UB is acceptable, and must not replace propagation where the pass should report the failure.

When combining two independent fallible interpreter operations, preserve deliberate precedence. The fixed code uses `self.pop_stack_frame_raw(unwinding).and(copy_ret_result)?` because 'An error here takes precedence over the copy error', instead of reporting `copy_ret_result?` after the frame pop.
Likewise, `self.get_ptr_alloc_mut(mplace.ptr(), size).and(misalign_res)?` keeps the allocation-access error over the misalignment error ('An error from get_ptr_alloc_mut takes precedence').

KnownPanicsLint's `use_ecx` maps the error through `trace!` and asserts that it is not a formatted-string error before discarding; direct `.ok()?` consumption of `layout_of` errors bypasses that diagnostic assertion.
The guard is deliberately silenced while the thread is already panicking to avoid a double panic, so a silently discarded error nested inside another panic will not produce the guard message.
analysis.testStrategy: Construct small Rust inputs that force each pass's speculative interpreter calls to fail, e.g. projections with invalid indices, invalid enum discriminants/niches, casts or arithmetic that raise interpreter errors, and constant-eval failures. Under a compiler built with the guard, a deliberately discarded error must take the conservative fallback (Top/None) without a guard panic, while an accidental plain `.ok()`/implicit drop should panic with the guard message rather than silently miss UB. Add paired cases where two fallible operations both fail to check that the expected error wins (frame-pop over return-copy; allocation-access over misalignment). Do not claim these tests were executed; no compiler was built for this analysis.
